central_topic: Minimal removal sets (verified by exact Bradley-Terry refit) that flip pairwise-comparison leaderboard rankings, and how the budget differs between crowd-vote (Chatbot Arena), expert/LLM-judge (MT-Bench) and sports (NBA Elo) comparison data.
core_methods: Bradley-Terry maximum-likelihood fitting on pairwise outcome counts
first-order influence / approximate maximum influence perturbation for data-dropping robustness
greedy removal search with exact-refit verification, prefix bisection and swap polish
cell-aggregated (pair-count) weighted refits with relaxed removal search
stationarity-LP over target ratings for minimal removal sets
comparators: influence-function and AMIP-style dropping-data robustness metrics
vote-rigging and adversarial manipulation of crowdsourced leaderboards
benchmarks: MT-Bench human expert and GPT-4 judgments
architectural_shifts: row-level influence greedy to cell-aggregated weighted refits
myopic first-order search to relaxed implicit-gradient / LP-based target-rating search with exact rounding and fallback
result_driven_themes: large crowd-vote tables flip with a tiny removal fraction while the small expert-judgment table resisted flipping within the removal cap in the search phase
influence-guided removal is far tighter than random removal, and permuted-outcome controls need larger budgets than real data
three search variants tied on the search-stage score, so the exact-refit-verified greedy is already near the achievable budget on the large crowd table
flip budget depends on the score gap relative to noise and on the evaluation design

queries.query: Bradley-Terry model paired comparisons maximum likelihood estimation ranking
queries.rationale: Defines the scoring model refit exactly in every flip-budget verification; needs the original model paper and standard MLE/fitting references.

queries.query: approximate maximum influence perturbation dropping small fraction of data robustness
queries.rationale: Closest methodological antecedent: first-order influence to find a small data subset whose removal changes a conclusion, which the greedy search re-linearises and verifies exactly.
Source of the influence-function machinery underlying the greedy removal ranking; reviewers will expect it as the first-order comparator.

queries.query: Chatbot Arena open platform evaluating LLMs human preference
queries.rationale: Describes the crowd-vote data (55k/140k battles) and the Bradley-Terry ranking pipeline being stress-tested.

queries.query: judging LLM-as-a-judge MT-Bench human expert pairwise judgments
queries.rationale: Provides the expert-judgment and GPT-4 judge comparison data, the small contrasting evaluation design with only a few models.

queries.query: improving model ranking Chatbot Arena vote rigging
queries.rationale: Adversarial manipulation of crowd votes is the deliberate-perturbation counterpart to the minimal-removal flip budgets reported.

queries.query: leaderboard illusion Chatbot Arena evaluation practices sampling private testing
queries.rationale: Documents data-access and sampling asymmetries that affect the same leaderboard, relevant for interpreting small flip budgets as fragility.

queries.query: adversarial manipulation robustness rank aggregation from pairwise comparisons
queries.rationale: Comparator literature on how few corrupted comparisons can change rankings from pairwise data, framing the removal-search results beyond LLM leaderboards.

queries.query: Elo rating system relation to Bradley-Terry sports game outcomes
queries.rationale: Connects the NBA Elo game-record data (sports evaluation design) to Bradley-Terry-type fitting, needed to justify cross-design comparison.

queries.query: statistical inference uncertainty ranking from pairwise comparisons confidence intervals bootstrap
queries.rationale: Flip budgets are interpreted against sampling noise (gap-to-noise); needs the ranking-uncertainty literature that leaderboard confidence intervals rely on.
